Desktop Publishing · Week 2 · Title

Setting up the page: size, orientation, margins

Before any design, set up the page: the paper size, which way up, and the margins that keep things safe.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Desktop Publishing · Week 2 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Name common paper sizes (A4, A5, A3)
  • Choose portrait or landscape
  • Set margins and know why they matter
Desktop Publishing · Week 2 · Idea 1

Understand it

A-sizes halve each time: A3 folded in half is A4; A4 folded is A5. A4 (210 × 297 mm) is the standard Nigerian document page; A5 is a handy flyer; A3 a small poster.

Orientation: portrait (tall) or landscape (wide). Choose by the content — a list is tall, a timeline is wide.

Margins are the empty border. They make a page look calm, stop text being cut off, and leave room for fingers. Keep at least 10–15 mm on a printed page. In Google Docs: File → Page setup; in Canva: choose a custom size in mm.

Desktop Publishing · Week 2 · Idea 2

Understand it

Decide the size FIRST: changing it later moves everything.

Desktop Publishing · Week 2 · Key words

Key words

A4
210 × 297 mm, the standard document page
Portrait / landscape
tall / wide orientation
Margin
the empty border around the page
Desktop Publishing · Week 2 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Fold an A4 sheet to make A5 and A6
  2. Set up an A5 portrait page in Canva or Docs
  3. Set 12 mm margins

Need a hand? Fold paper to feel the sizes before choosing one on screen.

Done early? Work out how many A6 cards fit on one A3 sheet, and why printers use that.

Desktop Publishing · Week 2 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • If you fold an A4 sheet in half, what size is each half?
  • Set up an A5 portrait page with 12 mm margins in Canva or Google Docs and show your instructor the settings.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
